title: Raising a Travel Credit Voucher on a Cancelled Air Ticket Fare Brands Booking
content:
Where a booking held in one of the Air Ticket Fare Brands has been cancelled, the value the ticket still carries may be put onto a travel credit voucher in the traveller's own name. This is the entry point for that voucher.

## 1. The situation this governs

The situation is a cancelled Air Ticket Fare Brands booking whose ticket still carries value. The result governed is the value placed on the voucher, and the effect the traveller sees is a voucher code they can quote against a future itinerary, together with the open travel credit standing on the booking.

## 2. The write that records it

The voucher is raised by the desk. The agent-side tool `issue_travel_credit_599fe29f` is unlocked and then called; one call mints a voucher code, posts a single credit-issue line carrying the stated value and the stated last redeemable date to that booking's ledger, and raises the booking's open travel credit by the same value.

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| air_booking_id | the internal reference number of the air booking whose remaining value goes onto the voucher, read from the traveller's booking record returned by the booking lookup | an identifier |
| customer_id | the traveller reference number the voucher is issued to, read from the traveller profile returned by the profile lookup | an identifier |
| voucher_value_usd | the value placed on the voucher | USD with exactly 2 decimal places, a positive number, rounded to the nearest cent at the moment it is passed; no empty value and no other currency |
| voucher_expires_on | the last calendar date on which the voucher may be redeemed | written as YYYY-MM-DD in the traveller's local calendar, with no time part and no empty value |

## 4. What comes back

A plain-language confirmation line naming the voucher code that was minted, the reference of the credit-issue line that carries it, the value placed on it in USD to two decimal places, and the last date it may be redeemed. The presence of the voucher code is what indicates the voucher now stands in the traveller's name; nothing is returned when no voucher is minted.
